# Best open-ear earbuds for running

These picks come from Runner's World, WIRED and SoundGuys testing. Prices are as listed in those articles and may have changed.

| Pick | Best for | Price | Key specs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** | Best overall clip-on, with the best sound | $199 (list $299) | 7 hrs (about 19.5 to 27 with case), IPX4, physical buttons |
| **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** | Best bone conduction, for maximum awareness | $125 to $180 | 12 hrs, IP55, physical buttons |
| **Shokz OpenDots 2** | Long runs and wet weather | $200 | 10 hrs (40 with case), IP57 |
| **Nothing Ear (Open)** | SoundGuys' pick for running, with strong bass | $99 at Amazon (list $149) | IP54, parametric EQ |
| **Soundcore AeroFit 2** | Budget | $79.99 at Amazon | IP55, long battery |
| **JLab Flex Open** | Cheapest way to try the clip-on style | about $40 | 7 hrs, IPX55 |

## Notes on the top picks

- **Bose Ultra Open:** WIRED praises its clear sound and the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-stride than touch controls. Runner's World says it's comfortable and doesn't bounce. It can be a bit quiet in heavy traffic, and Runner's World says Bose has a new pair coming soon, so you may want to wait or watch for discounts.
- **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2:** It has the most open feel because sound travels through your cheekbones. WIRED calls it "the best available" for runners who want more bass but still want to hear their surroundings. The neckband can clash with ponytails, hoods and winter hats, and the sound is less clear than the original OpenRun.
- **Shokz OpenDots 2:** WIRED's top overall pick. It survived rain and full submersion in testing, and it leaves the top of your ear free for glasses and hats.

## Where to buy

I can't pull direct retailer links for most of these, but each review has current buy buttons:
- Runner's World guide (Bose, Shokz, JLab and more): https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/
- WIRED guide (OpenDots 2, Aeroclip, Bose, Soundpeats PearlClip Pro at $50): https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/
- SoundGuys guide (Nothing Ear (Open), AeroFit 2): https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/
- Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 review, with REI and Best Buy links: https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/

**Soundcore AeroFit 2:** You can buy it through this affiliate link, which opens Soundcore's official US store: https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2. Dealectric lists it at $129.99, or $104 with code AFSC20, but SoundGuys shows it at $79.99 at Amazon. Compare prices before buying.

## Quick recommendation

- Want the best sound and comfort: **Bose Ultra Open**.
- Want maximum awareness on roads: **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2**.
- Run in rain or do long distances: **OpenDots 2**.
- Unsure about open-ear: **JLab Flex Open** or **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro** first.

Whichever you pick, keep the volume low enough to hear traffic. Open-ear designs help awareness but don't guarantee safety.
